title: Count material, state the boundary
hook: A heavier reusable container and light replacements accumulate material differently.

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Compare cumulative material amounts while stating what the account excludes.

misconception: A material-mass comparison alone proves the lower environmental impact.
objective: Compare cumulative material amounts while stating what the account excludes.

claims.text: A toy reusable container starts at 200g and uses 2g of replacement material/use. Single-use replacements each use 20g. Scaled model; toy masses; material only; no lifecycle claim.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Uses=10, A=220g and B=200g. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["+",200,["*",2,"x"]]; B=["*",20,"x"]; x denotes Uses. At x=10, A=220, B=200. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Include the starting material and the repeated additions within the chosen boundary. This toy mass account excludes energy, cleaning, transport and disposal; lower mass here does not establish a lower environmental impact.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["+",200,["*",2,"x"]]; B=["*",20,"x"]; x denotes Uses. At x=10, A=220, B=200. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits. claims.text: Toy mass account: a reusable container is 200g plus 2g per use; each single-use replacement is 20g. From how many uses is the reusable total lower? Correct: 12. At 11 uses it is 222g versus 220g; at 12 it is 224g versus 240g. Include the starting mass, and mass alone is not environmental impact.
